title: operations.dispatch.shipment.eway_requested
description: Operations asks finance to consider raising an e-Way bill for one carrier handover (Fulfilment ADR-0024 §6/plan F5, ADR-0019's stub adapter — `services/finance/app/eway/`). Fire-and-forget: operations never calls finance's e-Way machinery directly, and never re-implements e-Way validation itself. `consignment_value_minor` crossing operations' own coarse threshold mirror (₹50,000, `app.dispatch.services._EWAY_VALUE_THRESHOLD_MINOR`) is only a pre-filter so a trivial shipment never reaches this queue — the real 'is a bill required' call (`services/finance/app/domain.py::requires_eway_bill`, which also needs a document type, a supply type and a reported status this event carries none of) is finance's own, made from the invoice it already holds for this order. Money is integer minor units of `currency`.
$comment: Ahead of its consumer, the same shape operations.orders.order.invoice_requested was ahead of finance's invoice_requested_from_order before F4 landed: no services/finance consumer exists for this event yet (a documented follow-up — see the Fulfilment F5 slice's own report). This schema is the contract a future finance-side consumer should be built against, not a description of a consumer that exists today.

consignment_value_minor.description: The order's own total_minor at the moment of handover — the value finance's own requires_eway_bill threshold test is against, once it resolves this shipment against the invoice it holds.

dispatched_at.description: When the carrier took possession — the movement an e-Way bill, once raised, licenses.
